name: RestConnector

fields.label: API address
fields.description: The common part of the address records are read from, including any shared path prefix — e.g. 'api.example.com/v1'. The scheme is optional ('https://api.example.com/v1' means the same). The source name is appended to it.

fields.label: Records location
fields.description: Name of the field in the response body that holds the array of records — such as 'data', 'results', 'items'. Use dots for a nested field: 'payload.rows'.

fields.label: ID field
fields.description: Name of the field that uniquely identifies each record — 'id' in most APIs.

_comment: Generic REST connector. This file is installed as the connector's manifest exactly as written. connection and configSchema list the settings a person fills in when connecting: where the API lives, where the list of records sits in the response, and which field identifies a record. engine is a request template, not code; nothing in this file runs. The connector only reads from the external API; it never writes to it.

knowledge.purpose: Generic engine that reads records from the user's OWN HTTP API. The source name (entityType) is appended to the address; where the record array sits in the response and which field is the ID come from the connection settings, so an API that answers {data:[..]} and one that answers {results:[..]} share the same atom.
useCases: List data from the company's own REST service (products, branches, listings)
Reading from a public API (catalogue, exchange rates, weather)
Reading through a gateway placed in front of an internal service
capabilities: query (read; pagination via the engine's own query string)
knowledge.configSchema: connection.config = { baseUrl, itemsPath, idField } — the source name comes from entityType and is appended to the address
antiPatterns: A vendor API with its own connector engine (its own paging, site resolution or field flattening) — that engine belongs in the vendor's provider pack, not in this atom
Entities in the host's own database — that is the platform/entities capability's job; this atom is for external APIs

Writing credentials such as keys or passwords into the connection settings — credentials live in the project's auth binding and NEVER enter the pack; these fields say WHERE the source is, not WHO we are
